summary: Sketch mode shows the part behind the sketch, and can cut it at the sketch plane. While a sketch is open, the 3D view stays under the sketch canvas instead of being hidden, drawn through an orthographic camera that looks along the sketch plane's normal with the sketch's V axis up and the canvas's view box as its frustum, so every point of the part lands on the pixel of the matching sketch point and the sketch's pan and zoom move both together. Solids, the other sketches and curves are drawn; the open sketch draws itself, and planes, the grid, the axes and pick highlights stay out of the way. The View drawer below the dock gains 3D background, with Dimmed, the default, Normal and Hidden, and Cut part by sketch plane. Dimmed blends every drawn colour 62% toward the view's background gradient at that pixel and keeps depth, so the part reads as 3D and the open sketch stays dominant; Normal draws the part as in the 3D view; Hidden draws nothing behind the sketch, as before. The cut clips away everything on the viewer's side of the sketch plane, with a small tolerance that keeps faces lying on the plane, on the solids, their edges and the other sketches, without caps. The choices are remembered on the device for the next sketch and are not part of the document. The view behind the sketch draws only when the sketch view pans, zooms or resizes, or when the model, its lines or the choices change: hovering, dragging or drawing in the sketch draws no 3D frame. With Normal, the sketch strokes, the drawing previews and every stroke of the Trim, Extend and Split previews lie on a dark under-stroke in the theme background colour, a pixel wider on each side, so they stay readable on bright faces. The sketch canvas keeps every pointer, focus and keyboard input, and nothing in 3D can be picked during sketch mode: the 3D layer is inert, and focus the 3D view held moves to the sketch canvas however the sketch opens, from the tree, a double-click, an agent or undo, and back to the 3D view when it closes. Nothing moves the model camera while a sketch is open: a first build or a rebuild that grows the part uploads its geometry and widens only the sketch camera's depth range, and view commands reaching the covered view are refused. Leaving the sketch returns the model camera exactly as it was, and shows the planes and lines the sketch left out again without rebuilding them; only when the view showed nothing but planes before the sketch opened, and a first fit was asked for meanwhile, does leaving fit the part once.
warning: No breaking change for CAD files, installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output. Potentially breaking for automation that inspects the page in sketch mode: the 3D viewport element stays in the page behind the sketch canvas, as div.cad-viewport.is-sketch-background with aria-hidden="true", the inert attribute, pointer-events none and its canvas out of the tab order, where it was a hidden element; its graphics host carries data-cad-frames-drawn, a count of frames drawn. Selectors that expect no visible .cad-viewport or WebGL canvas during sketch mode, or that count canvas elements, must allow for it. Focus the 3D canvas held moves to the sketch canvas when a sketch opens and back to the 3D canvas when it closes, so automation that keeps the focused element must allow for it. Screenshots of sketch mode now show the part behind the sketch, dimmed by default, and in Normal the sketch strokes and the Trim, Extend and Split previews carry a dark under-stroke. In Normal each stroke of those three previews has a copy drawn beneath it with the same role class and cad-sketch-halo, so a selector such as .is-added or .is-retained inside a preview matches two elements there; exclude .cad-sketch-halo to find the stroke itself. The Arc tool's invalid-arc guide is now a g.cad-path-invalid group holding its polyline; captures through cad_capture_preview still show only the sketch. The View drawer in sketch mode gains a 3D background select and a Cut part by sketch plane check box, so automation that counts its controls or tab stops must allow for them. Device preferences under wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1 gain an optional sketchView field; releases 0.0.786 and earlier ignore it and drop it when they next write the preferences, which returns the choices to Dimmed and uncut.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage, journal or worker protocol change. Device preferences (localStorage wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1) gain an optional sketchView: {background: 'normal' | 'dimmed' | 'hidden', cutBySketchPlane: boolean}; a value this release cannot read is ignored and the other preferences stay in force, and stored bytes are never rewritten except by an explicit choice. The view state is modelled in src/features/cad/view/cadViewState.ts as a part or sketch context with background, cut and a pick scope that is only 'sketch' for now, so a later section view and selection filter extend it. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. The sketch canvas publishes its view box through a camera link outside React whenever the view frame changes; the link drops a view equal to the last one, and the viewport draws at most one frame per animation frame when a new view arrives. A frame is drawn behind the sketch only for a new view, a changed model, changed lines behind the sketch, a resize or a changed choice; a new document version that leaves the lines the same, as a sketch edit does, draws nothing. The viewport behind the sketch publishes no viewport controls, so WebMCP viewport commands and captures in sketch mode reach the sketch canvas as before. The lines the open sketch leaves out of its background, the planes and its own lines, are kept out of the scene with their buffers and shader programs while it is open, so leaving the sketch shows them again without rebuilding them; a line changed meanwhile is rebuilt, as before. While a sketch covers the model view, the model camera does not move: the first fit a first build or first references ask for waits, and runs on leaving only if the view showed nothing but planes when the sketch opened; otherwise it is dropped, and later rebuilds never fit, as before. This includes Hidden, which in 0.0.786 and earlier fitted a first solid built during the sketch; a later build with larger bounds widens the sketch camera's depth range only. Covered view controls refuse fit and standard views, and the model view's keyboard context menu does not open while covered. When the covering sketch surface changes, focus inside the covered 3D view, or on nothing, moves to the sketch canvas; when the last surface closes, focus left on nothing moves to the 3D canvas; focus elsewhere, such as a tree row, stays. A region pick shows the 3D view itself, as before; a sketch reference pick or a profile copy preview, which draw their own sketch surface, still hide the part behind it, as before.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added, removed or changed. The View drawer in sketch mode adds 3D background (Normal, Dimmed, Hidden) and Cut part by sketch plane, which is disabled while the background is Hidden, with help that says picks reach only the open sketch and that the choices stay on this device. A Pick only in current sketch control is left out: a disabled check box cannot take focus, so its help would be unreachable, and the pick scope is stated in the help instead. The exact section outline from the solid kernel is left out: the kernel section supports principal planes only and would need a new worker request per build and plane, which is more risk than this change carries; the cut shows the section edge where the clipped faces end. The shared UI components and theme are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. The sketch view choices live only in the device preference key above, in browser local storage, and are not saved in documents, the browser cache workbench or the folder adapter.
checklist.verification: New unit suites: cadViewState (reducer, remembered choices, reading stored choices field by field), cadSketchCamera (every sketch point on its canvas pixel within 0.001 px at several zooms and pans on principal, offset, datum and flipped planes; view direction, up and depth range; the cut for both senses of the normal; the camera link drops equal views), cadSketchBackgroundStyle (the dim blend in lit, basic and dashed shaders, one shared amount and one program for Normal and Dimmed, and reuse of unchanged background references), cadPreferences (sketchView stored with the other preferences; an unreadable value ignored without dropping the rest). CadViewport: drawing only through the sketch camera and only for a new view, model, lines or choice, one frame per pan or zoom step, none for a repeated view or Hidden, the dim and cut uniforms and planes with local clipping on, the model camera restored exactly; no frame for a new document version with the same lines; lines left out of the background kept aside and shown again unrebuilt, a line edited meanwhile replaced, and set-aside lines disposed with the view; the layer behind the sketch inert, and the keyboard context menu opening only once the model view shows; in Dimmed and in Hidden, the model camera's position, rotation, up, zoom and frustum unchanged through a first build and a rebuild 15 times taller during the sketch and through fit and Front from controls held from before, the sketch camera's depth range growing with the part, and the same camera in Isometric after leaving; with only planes shown before the sketch, the part framed once on leaving and that framing kept through a later sketch and rebuild. CadSketchViewModes: the workbench shows the part dimmed, switches Normal, Hidden and the cut from the View drawer and stores them, opens the next sketch with them; hover, a box drag, Line hover and a Line drag that commits publish no view and hand the viewport nothing new, and one wheel step publishes one view; focus in the 3D view, or on nothing, moving to the sketch canvas when an agent, the tree or Hidden opens a sketch, the sketch then handling F, and back to the 3D view when it closes, while focus on a tree row stays there; the under-stroke drawn first and wider within each edge and profile and under a Line drag preview in Normal only. Chromium spec cad-sketch-view-modes: pixel probes at sketch coordinates for Normal, Dimmed (0.15 to 0.6 of Normal) and Hidden, the cut in Normal and Dimmed removing a raised block and keeping the plate, no 3D frame during hover, a box drag or Line hover and exactly one per wheel step, the background aria-hidden, without pointer events and out of the tab order, and the model camera and plane labels restored after finishing; in Normal both sketch strokes on an under-stroke in the theme background colour that takes no pointer, none in Dimmed or Hidden. A second test focuses the 3D canvas, opens a sketch by agent and finds the layer inert, the sketch canvas as document.activeElement, a wheel zoom and F reaching the sketch, and the 3D canvas focused again after finishing; a third opens a sketch over a document with no body, builds the first solids and then a block grown to 100 mm, and finds the model camera, zoom and plane labels exactly as before the sketch after finishing. Mutations, each caught: dropping the on-demand guard in the viewport (unit frame-count tests; the spec never settles), publishing every canvas render (link, viewport and workbench tests; the spec sees frames during hover), breaking the camera sync (pixel test, viewport test; the spec loses the block in Normal), dropping the material clipping planes or turning local clipping off (viewport tests; the spec still sees the block with the cut), disposing instead of setting aside (the set-aside test). Review round 1: no inert and no focus handover (viewport lifecycle and workbench focus tests; the focus spec finds no inert attribute); inert kept without the handover (workbench focus test; the focus spec finds body focused instead of the sketch canvas); automatic fits and covered fit and standard views moving the model camera (both camera cases; the camera spec sees zoom 1.0487 become 1.0370 and a plane label move 58 px); no fit on leaving after planes only (the framing test); the under-stroke drawn in Dimmed instead of Normal (the halo test). Review round 2: CadSketchCanvas checks that in Normal the Extend, Split and Trim previews draw one under-stroke per stroke, with the same role and shape, all before the strokes and taking no pointer, and none without the outline; the view-modes spec opens Extend end over a plate in Normal and finds the added piece drawn 2 px with 5 px and 3 px dashes over a 4 px under-stroke in the theme background colour with the same dashes and no pointer. Mutation: the Extend preview without the outline setting fails the CadSketchCanvas test. After review round 2, the CadSketchCanvas, CadSketchCanvasRender, CadSketchViewModes, CadWorkbench and cadPathDrawing suites (318 tests), npm run build, oxlint, npm run ui:check, check-release and cad-sketch-view-modes (4 tests, run alone) passed. Checks after review round 1: full Vitest 6688 of 6688 passed in 566 files; npm run build including the e2e type-check and the documentation check; oxlint with zero findings; npm run ui:check; check-release passes. Chromium specs, each run alone with two workers on the final build after review round 1: cad-sketch-view-modes 3, cad-sketch-constraints 28, cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7, cad-intersecting-areas 1, cad-kernel 2, cad-region-workflow 1, cad-sketch-arc-extend 1, cad-sketch-arc-trim 1, cad-sketch-axis-dimension 1, cad-sketch-circle-trim 1, cad-sketch-concentric 1, cad-sketch-context-editing 1, cad-sketch-dimension-placement 1, cad-sketch-dimension-points 1, cad-sketch-dimension-selection 4, cad-sketch-editing 2, cad-sketch-line-chain 1, cad-sketch-linear-pattern 1, cad-sketch-midpoint 1, cad-sketch-mirror-copy 1, cad-sketch-offset 2, cad-sketch-persistent-reference 1, cad-sketch-placed-dimensions 1, cad-sketch-placement 1, cad-sketch-point-on-line 1, cad-sketch-profile-copy 1, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions 1, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 1, cad-sketch-symmetry 1, cad-sketch-tangent-joint 1, cad-topology-repick 3, cad-workflow 32; 32 specs and 106 tests, all passed. Measurements at 4x CPU in Chromium with SwiftShader on 60 constrained rectangles, recorded in docs/maintainers/cad-performance.md: no 3D frame during any hover; Select hover P50 within 20.2 to 22.5 ms in every mode; Line hover P50 3 ms higher in Dimmed than Hidden in two early sessions, 11.5 ms higher in a quiet review session and equal (36.8 against 36.7 ms) in the next, so the gap is not established as a cost of the view behind the sketch, and an opaque WebGL context (35.6 and 40.0 ms against 34.0 and 36.8 ms) and a still image of the frame (38.0 and 42.3 ms) were tried and not adopted; the Normal under-stroke within the spread of single runs (Line 33.4 ms with it, 31.4 ms without); exit from Dimmed 51 ms against 55 ms in Hidden after keeping the left-out lines aside, where it was 89 against 40 ms before; heap, DOM nodes, listeners and canvases unchanged over 10 enter and exit cycles. After merging main at 7ef7b715 (0.0.786): full Vitest 6730 of 6730 passed in 571 files; npm run build, oxlint with zero findings and npm run ui:check pass; check-release passes against origin/main; cad-sketch-view-modes (4) and cad-sketch-constraints (28), each run alone with two workers, passed.

publicNotes.summary: The part stays visible behind a sketch, and can be cut at the sketch plane.
changes: While you edit a sketch, the part and the other sketches stay visible behind it, lined up with the sketch, and pan and zoom with it.

Open View below the dock to set 3D background to Dimmed, the default, Normal or Hidden. In Normal, sketch lines and the previews of drawing, Trim, Extend and Split get a dark edge so they stay readable on bright faces.
Cut part by sketch plane removes everything on your side of the sketch plane, so you see the part where the sketch lies.

Your choices are remembered in this browser for the next sketch. Clicks, drags and keys still reach only the sketch, which takes keyboard focus from the 3D view when it opens, and leaving the sketch returns the 3D view as you left it.
publicNotes.compatibility: No file, schema or tool change. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: No action is needed. Automation that inspects sketch mode must allow for the 3D view element behind the sketch canvas and the two new View controls.
